subject: vectorized rats model + variation in run times

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: vectorized rats model + variation in run times
parts:
Damn. Not as much potential for vectorization
as I was recalling on the train. But I did
replace the (sigma * sigma) with square(sigma)
and (x - mu) * (x - mu) with square(x-mu) in
the definition of the normal_log functions.

What I have now for the normal samples is:

data
double y[N,T];

params
double alpha[N];
double beta[N];

BEFORE:

for (n in 1:N) {
alpha[n] ~ normal(mu_alpha, sigma_alpha);
beta[n] ~ normal(mu_beta, sigma_beta);
for (t in 1:T)
y[n,t] ~ normal(alpha[n] + beta[n] * (x[t] - xbar), sigma_y);
}

AFTER:

alpha ~ normal(mu_alpha, sigma_alpha); // vectorized
beta ~ normal(mu_beta, sigma_beta); // vectorized
for (n in 1:N)
for (t in 1:T)
y[n,t] ~ normal(alpha[n] + beta[n] * (x[t] - xbar), sigma_y);

I couldn't vectorize the y[n,t], because there's a varying
slope and varying intercept, so the gains from vectorization
here are going to be modest (they reduce the N logarithm
calcs and auto-difs in the alpha[n] and beta[n] samples to one).
But the squares do make some headway because they reduce the
size of memory and the number of allocations and stack ops we
need for auto-dif.

Profiling, the time's almost all taken in computing logs and in
pushing auto-dif variables onto and off of the stack.

I'm also seeing a huge amount of variance run to run,
which Matt thinks may have to do with the auto-tuning.
I'm getting everything from 3.5s to 15s in a set of
about ten runs. So that'd leave JAGS 15-times to 75-times
faster for this example.

Needless to say, Matt's going to look into the root causes
of the variation. We need to find the right answers and figure
out if we're at least getting those despite the time variations.
Ideally, we'll be able to reduce the inter-run variation in
time taken. Intuitively, if the optimization gives you different
results, NUTS may need to run the leapfrog integrator for differing
number of steps.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] vectorized rats model + variation in run times
parts:
We weren't measuring the inter-run variation.
The changes didn't add the variation, additional
measurement just brought it to light. It's
calculating exactly the same gradient, just
a bit more efficiently, so the changes aren't
even visible to NUTS.

- Bob

On 11/9/11 7:58 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> If Stan was 50 times slower than Jags before, I can't see how it can be 75 times slower now! In any case, some auto-tunig should help a lot. Ideally it would do about 3, not 75, I think.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: vectorized rats model + variation in run times
parts:
General comment about speed: Anything that links against the Eigen
library should have the -DNDEBUG flag passed to the compiler. That
disables range checking for Eigen matrices / vectors / arrays.

Ben
